scope: current shared I3/G2B runtime deploy workflow trigger-to-authorization reconciliation

findings.summary: The current shared runtime deploy workflow watches I3 legal, original G2-B and G2-B recovery execute paths, but its authorization step requires an exact one-file diff equal to the recovery execute file and validates the recovery request/execute lineage and one-shot state before provider authentication. Therefore a push that changes the historical I3 or original G2-B marker cannot cross the authorization boundary. A recovery-marker push also cannot proceed with the current recovery request because it is disabled and consumed.
findings.f1F2Treatment: Preserve historical evidence but normalize/tombstone stale event-marker enabled/consumed fields so they cannot be mistaken for current authority. Canonical state remains continuity lock + terminal receipt + consumed ledger.

findings.summary: Five write/deploy-capable Corte6 execute artifacts inspected in this tranche are terminal, enabled=false and consumed=true. Historical writes/deploys recorded by some markers remain evidence only and do not constitute current authorization.

M8 and M10 remain enabled historical execute artifacts, but their declared modes and budgets are read-only and explicitly set provider/data/deploy mutation budgets to zero. They do not expand the write-capable surface, although F2 should make current-vs-historical authority unambiguous.

backend/config/m9-provider-precutover-readonly-execute.json is misleadingly named readonly but declares mode ONE_RETRY_PROMOTION_REAL_ROOT_SMOKE_CONDITIONAL_ROLLBACK, maxProductionPromotions=1 and maxConditionalRollbacks=1 while enabled=true and consumed=false under an August 13 authorization. This is historical authority that must not survive into the canonical control-plane. No execution is authorized now and no provider mutation was performed in this tranche.
findings.f1Treatment: Terminalize/inertize the historical M9 promotion/rollback authority while preserving immutable evidence; ensure no workflow/tool can treat this artifact as current authorization.
findings.relationship: Concrete unresolved member of CP117 historicalGlobalExhaustive=false; counted as a specific newly classified HOLD, not as a new methodology.

reconciliations.CP117: REMAINS_OPEN; M9 proves the historical one-shot ledger is not globally exhaustive.
reconciliations.CP118: REMAINS_EXISTING_CONTROL_DRIFT; cxorbia-evidence-aliases.json is non-executable but still carries syncEpoch 47 while continuity lock is epoch 50. No duplicate finding added.
reconciliations.G2B: UNCHANGED_TERMINAL_RECOVERY_NO_PROVIDER_SIDE_EFFECT; no retry/replay; F3 still required after F0/F1/F2.
